ai.title: What VP ≠ VNP Means
ai.summary: The Anthropic proof that VP≠VNP means that there is no way to find the permanent of a matrix of 0s and 1s if we are limited to arithmetic circuits of size polynomial in the input-size. This means that for P to equal NP, there must be some trick to computing permanents using AND/OR/NOT on the bits of the input that is better than addition and multiplication. There are many problems where access to Boolean operators is helpful, but it isn't clear how they would help with the permanent. There is a $1 million prize for a solution to this problem.

infosec.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ASP.NET Anti-CSRF Library Flaw Allowing Unauthenticated RCE

Mandiant found the bug and confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, but no patch is coming for versions 0.9.1.0 and 0.9.1 Beta. Defenders should search Web.config files and bin/ directories for AntiCsrfModule references, replace the library with System.Web.Helpers.AntiForgery or ASP.NET Core IAntiforgery, and rotate machineKey and other secrets if IIS logs show unusual .aspx POSTs returning 302 or 500.

The company hasn't disclosed how attackers gained access, when the activity occurred, or whether student or institutional data was taken. It has said only that the affected systems contain no government IDs or financial data, and no ransomware group has claimed responsibility. Until Turnitin discloses the scope, institutions should watch for phishing attempts using Turnitin as a lure and review their SSO and LMS integration logs for unusual access.

infosec.title: Brake Check: Hijacking Trailer Brakes Over Bluetooth
infosec.summary: Researchers found that Elecbrakes EB2, VM1, and ELBC 2000 trailer brake controllers accepted unauthenticated Bluetooth commands. A nearby phone or laptop could write four bytes to activate, modulate, or release trailer brakes without pairing, a PIN, or authorization. The force byte controlled braking strength, and nearly every non-zero opcode activated the brakes. Commands lacked replay protection, and a persistent register retained the last command. The firmware-update channel used Just Works pairing, CRC32 integrity checks, and an app-distributed decryption key. Elecbrakes fixed EB2 and VM1 on July 6. ELBC 2000 remains unpatched. CISA assigned CVE-2026-96805, CVE-2026-125273, and CVE-2026-124281.

infosec.title: Judge the Cyber Apocalypse by the Data, Not the Headlines
infosec.summary: CSET's Andrew Lohn finds that while the technical indicators favor attackers, with monthly CVEs tripling since Claude Mythos launched, slower patching, and exploitation now behind 31% of breaches, data on real-world impact looks steady or better, since significant incidents, healthcare breach victims, breach costs, and ransomware payouts are all flat or down. He explains that fear of attribution and retaliation, not technical capability, may have always limited nation-states and criminals. He recommends tougher enforcement, investment in attribution and resilience, and hardening critical systems for a crisis where those limits fall away, but he concedes that some datasets lag and the trend could still turn.

infosec.title: AI Agents Are Creating a Shared Responsibility Gap
infosec.summary: Shared responsibility models have been a staple framework for SaaS and cloud services, delineating which aspects a provider is responsible for and which a user is responsible for. Harnesses and the MCP spec both put the responsibility and audit logging for sensitive actions on the user. Agent identities also do not provide a silver bullet. For example, Microsoft's documentation for Entra agent identities also puts responsibility for sensitive actions back on the user. Organizations must accept that responsibility cannot be delegated and that agents require clear owners, least privilege, and consistent logging.

infosec.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
infosec.summary: Shirudo is an open-source eBPF runtime from OpenAI and Cisco that deploys temporary "shields" to block a vulnerable code path on a running Linux system without a restart or a patch. In a test, a shield generated by Codex added an input check to Java's Base64 decoder and stopped a Java4Shell exploit against a live Elasticsearch process. Shields are cryptographically signed, checked by the eBPF verifier, and recorded through TPM attestation, which makes Shirudo a promising stopgap for teams with long patch cycles, though the case for AI-generated shields so far rests on a single controlled demo.

infosec.title: Here's Why Data Breach Disclosure is so Hard: Lessons from Hundreds of Emails with Hacked Companies
infosec.summary: Troy Hunt reviewed 8.5 years of breach-notification emails sent to 73 organizations. Common responses included no security contact, denial before reviewing evidence, open-ended investigations, legal control of wording, and arguments that disclosure itself causes harm. In one case, leaked records covered 16 user-system tables, including identity-verification and tax documents. Effective organizations replied quickly, investigated the evidence, notified customers, and published updates.

infosec.title: What 5,400 Malicious npm Packages Reveal about Software Supply Chain Risk in 2026
infosec.summary: A review of about 5,400 malicious npm packages from the past year found that compromised legitimate packages made up only 7% of the set but more than 99% of downloads, while the attacker-created packages that make up most of the malware were rarely installed at all. After npm revoked long-lived tokens, attackers moved to compromising CI pipelines and publishing through OIDC trusted publishing, and 38% of packages hid their C2 traffic in legitimate services such as Cloudflare Workers and Discord webhooks. The registry took a median of 7 days to remove malicious packages, while attackers often deleted their own within hours.

design.title: Forward-Deployed Design As Plumbing
design.summary: Forward-deployed design positions designers as hands-on problem solvers who address underlying organizational and operational issues rather than simply improving interfaces. As AI makes software development more accessible, the greatest obstacles to improving public services increasingly involve coordination between institutions, governance, permissions, and competing responsibilities. Experimental public-service prototypes developed in a University of Michigan classroom demonstrate how designers can use functional software to expose these institutional barriers and explore practical solutions.

A design check would then run inside the coding agent's loop and again in CI, flagging low scores for a designer.

design.title: The AI Problems Nobody Has Solved Yet
design.summary: An internal UX assessment of Meta AI across Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp revealed fundamental challenges in evaluating experiences that produce unpredictable responses. Traditional usability methods struggle to accommodate inconsistent outputs, variable response times, and hallucinations that appear just as convincing as accurate information. Designing effective AI experiences requires new approaches to evaluating model performance, communicating uncertainty, managing user expectations, and establishing responsibility for detecting errors.

design.summary: An open-source handwriting animation library for any font. Tegaki extracts each glyph's strokes, their order and width, and draws them stroke by stroke on a canvas over real, selectable text.

design.summary: Prompt inside the canvas, drop in a doc, or write it in code, and watch the diagram build itself.

design.title: This beautiful logo design was created to grow like nature
design.summary: Philadelphia-based Smith & Diction has redesigned the Pennsylvania Horticultural Society's identity ahead of its 200th anniversary, replacing a generic tree emblem with a dynamic representation of plant life. The new PHS lettermark acts as a root system from which different native plants grow, with illustrations by Summer McClure arranged within rectangles inspired by Philadelphia's street grid. Frame-by-frame animations by Henrique Barone depict plants growing from the letterforms, while additional animations and a printed flipbook bring the identity's organic movement to life.

design.title: How Material Constraints Sharpen Design Thinking for Physical Projects
design.summary: Budget, environment, and lifespan give designers concrete criteria for revisiting choices made on screen before anything goes to production. Pentagram's bronze drain covers, PUMA's Clever Little Bag with 65% less cardboard than a shoebox, and the Eames plywood chair show constraints shaping form. Full-size samples, each testing one defined question, settle what flat layouts and renderings leave open.

design.title: Lighting That Feels Just Right
design.summary: Real-time global illumination supplies what simple Blinn-Phong lighting lacks: light that bounces, bleeds color, and tints neighboring surfaces. Screen-Space Global Illumination comes first, followed by a more practical probe-based approach to estimating indirect light in browser-based 3D scenes. Reflections, sky light, volumetric lighting, and atmospheric scattering are then layered on for the finished look.

design.title: I Dare Apple to Make this Delightful AirPods Design a Reality
design.summary: Concept artist Anand Krishnavi's "AirPods G3" are based on the iMac G3 and use colorful translucent plastic that shows the parts inside, unlike Apple's white-only in-ear AirPods.

design.title: Inside Ava Roth's Artistic Collaboration with Thousands of Tiny Bee Workers
design.summary: Artist Ava Roth places broken ceramics, frames, textiles, and embroidery hoops inside beehives, where bees bind the pieces together with honeycomb.

design.title: Font vs typeface: the ultimate guide
design.summary: A typeface describes a shared visual design across a family of characters, while a font traditionally refers to a particular weight, width, and style or its corresponding digital file, although variable fonts have blurred this distinction by combining multiple styles within a single file.

marketing.title: Is your free AI visibility report just another meaningless metric?
marketing.summary: It seems like everybody's shipping some kind of "try before you buy" AI visibility tool. But most of these risk falling into the trap of yet-another-number that's hard to interpret - and even harder to act on. marketing.title: Accenture Life Trends 2027
marketing.summary: Consumers are embracing innovation while seeking more human connection and control. AI-generated content is driving interest in human-made media and private communities. Concerns about technology's impact on local communities are increasing demand for transparency and accountability. Biotech breakthroughs are raising healthcare expectations while AI and digital platforms help people build independent income streams. Meanwhile, wellness culture is fueling fatigue as constant self-improvement becomes exhausting.

marketing.title: Wikipedia explainers lost a median 40% of views since 2022, biographies lost 9%
marketing.summary: Explainer pages that an AI answer can cover in two lines lost the most traffic, while pages about people held up. For instance, photosynthesis fell from 79,000 monthly views to 45,000, and Napoleon only slipped from 365,000 to 346,000. Nearly all of the topic decline came in the two years after Google launched AI Overviews, and the pre-2022 trend of about 5% drop a year explains only half of it.

marketing.title: Why many people who can pay upfront are choosing to pay over time
marketing.summary: Consumers increasingly use buy now, pay later products to manage cash flow and preserve savings, even when they can afford to pay upfront. In the survey, 58% of deferred-payment users had used these products to keep money in savings or investments, while 47% of financed transactions could have been paid upfront. Fixed payment schedules also appeal to consumers, as 57% prefer predictable payments over flexible, open-ended credit. These patterns show how credit products can serve different financial needs, from avoiding credit card interest to covering expenses while waiting for a paycheck.

marketing.title: Your AI already has your brand doc. Here's why the drafts are still generic
marketing.summary: AI drafts often sound generic because brand guidelines rely on vague adjectives instead of specific customer and product knowledge. Build a one-page “Brand Brain” with customer pain points in their own words and value propositions backed by proof. Include what your product does and doesn't do alongside an unedited writing sample. Test it by running the same prompt with and without this context. Compare the results and refine the document wherever the output still sounds generic or makes unsupported claims.

marketing.title: Google's ‘Top 10' Line for CMOs Points at Generic Tips Posts
marketing.summary: Google is urging brands to replace generic ‘tips' posts with content built on first-hand expertise. Its example contrasts a generic “Top 10 Things to Consider” article with a detailed analysis of why a specific customer's running shoes failed. The guidance also encourages brands to optimize for conversational searches rather than just keywords and measure performance through leads and sales instead of proxy metrics. Google Search's own AI guide makes the same distinction between common knowledge and original experience.

marketing.title: How is AI changing the future of GTM?
marketing.summary: Tech product marketing and GTM leaders can explore this and other key challenges across 70+ sessions at Gartner Product Leadership Conference 2027 (March 8–9, Grapevine, TX). Topics include agentic AI and revenue generation, evolving enterprise buying behaviors, and commercial content. See the agenda

marketing.title: Snipd
marketing.summary: Snipd helps users capture and revisit insights while listening. Tapping your headphones saves a podcast segment with its audio, transcript, and AI-generated summary. Users can also chat with episodes to find specific information and get answers. Highlights can be exported to tools like Notion, Readwise, and Obsidian for future reference.

marketing.title: “Made with AI” ads hurt your brand
marketing.summary: AI disclosure labels can hurt ad performance and brand perception, especially when brands explain why they used AI. Across three experiments, 82% to 92% of people who noticed an AI label assumed the company used AI primarily to benefit itself, such as cutting costs. Explanations about improving quality or benefiting consumers did little to change that perception and made people rate ads less favorably. Avoid using AI for emotional brand messaging, where consumers are 24.6% less likely to recommend the brand, and use it instead to refine creative ideas or support post-production. If disclosure is required, keep the label simple rather than explaining your reasons for using AI.

marketing.title: Consumers, oblivious of being targeted, find online ads helpful
marketing.summary: Telling people why they're seeing an ad made them feel more watched, even when the ad wasn't retargeted at all. Retargeting itself mostly landed as helpful, raising click intention as ads for a product viewed earlier followed people across sites. The more sites those ads appeared on, though, the stronger the sense of surveillance and the worse people felt about ads. Offering controls over ad topics alongside the explanation could offset that effect.

marketing.title: Craft first, AI second
marketing.summary: AI should support design craft rather than replace it. Start by sketching ideas and refining features before turning to AI for building and iteration. Too many tools and constant reviewing can create cognitive overload. A focused workflow with 2-3 tools is more manageable. Better results also come from precise prompts instead of vague instructions. Build a library of inspiring screenshots and interactions. Save feedback and design decisions to help AI better match your taste and reduce back-and-forth.

marketing.title: Download LinkedIn connections before Dec. 2
marketing.summary: Download your LinkedIn connections before December 2 to preserve job titles and company data, and save an unmodified copy for future reference.

marketing.title: Why confusing ads still work
marketing.summary: Viewers who see their own problem in an ad want to learn more even when they can't say what the product does, so copy should describe the customer's situation rather than the company.

marketing.title: Airlines Are Turning Their Passenger Data Into Media Networks
marketing.summary: Knowing where and when passengers travel makes airline audiences valuable to brands, but the same precision risks making passengers feel followed.

founders.title: AI Is a Customer Repellent
founders.summary: Companies have significantly raised AI spending in customer service without much return. People are more likely to take their problems to third-party AI providers than to talk to company-owned chatbots. Use AI where it makes things better without asking anyone to talk to it.

founders.title: Inside the Pay-Per-Job AI Business Model
founders.summary: Startups selling AI work have to decide who pays for retries and unusable results. An operator building an AI research product compares charging for effort against charging for a delivered output or a successful outcome. Candor bills per synthetic interview while buyers think in studies of 15 to 24 interviews, so the cost unit differs from what customers buy. True gross profit per paid job must include retries and free trials alongside model costs and human review. Repeat demand follows a natural cycle, so teams should wait that full window before judging a cohort.

founders.title: The AI slop era rewards one thing…
founders.summary: Picking creators by follower count often misses real engagement in feeds full of AI content. Cal AI evaluated more than 10,000 creators and signed over 300. The company looked for real conversations in a creator's comments rather than follower count or emoji replies. Cal AI paid creators fully upfront to earn their trust. Test hooks cheaply with AI-generated creative and then film the winning concepts with real people before scaling.

founders.title: Why confusing ads still work
founders.summary: Ads and landing pages can still spark interest even when readers do not fully understand them. A growth firm reanalyzed user-test responses and measured whether people wanted to learn more. Actual understanding explained 3% of the variation in interest, while relatability explained 58%. Relatability was the strongest predictor in these tests, so audit your copy by counting sentences about your company against sentences about the customer's situation. Then show the message to a small group of target customers and ask who they think it is for.

Standard usage is free within published quotas, while agents must switch from direct REST APIs to MCP by February 1, 2027, with Scaled tier billing starting April 1, 2027.

founders.summary: 10-minute walks when a coding agent starts going in circles, foot pedals to screenshot bugs, rambling voice notes that then get edited down. Add yours →

founders.title: SaaS that Survives
founders.summary: There's always been a category of software that existed to only serve the niche of 'software skill gap'. People buy software to get a job done when the ROI on figuring out the task themselves never really pays off. AI now makes it possible for people to build their own solutions. While the game has certainly changed, there's still plenty of opportunity to build software companies.

crypto.title: Kalshi halts Utah operations while avoiding immediate ban in New York
crypto.summary: Kalshi paused operations in Utah, where it had 177,000 users, after a federal judge let the state enforce its gambling laws. It is waiting on a ruling on the CFTC's request to block Utah from enforcing against it. In New York, Justice Melissa Crane denied the Attorney General's request for a temporary restraining order, saying the questions around derivatives and preemption are complex. Kalshi had warned the order could shut it down nationwide. The CFTC and DOJ have also sued Utah, Arkansas, Louisiana, and New York over state enforcement against prediction markets.

crypto.title: CFTC Staff Advisory Permits Crypto Assets to Count Toward Financial Resources Requirements
crypto.summary: The CFTC issued a staff advisory on permitting derivatives trading platforms and clearinghouses to count bitcoin, ether, and payment stablecoins toward the one-year operating cost coverage component of their financial resources requirements. Firms must still hold cash or highly liquid securities to satisfy a separate liquidity requirement, so crypto assets cannot fully replace traditional capital reserves under the framework. Prior CFTC rules were silent on whether crypto counted toward the operating cost threshold, leaving registered entities without clear guidance on how to treat native asset holdings on their balance sheets. The advisory, issued under Chairman Mike Selig, reflects the CFTC's approach of using staff guidance to extend crypto clarity in derivatives markets without full rulemaking cycles.

crypto.title: Ethereum Foundation Doubles Security Team for Post-Quantum Overhaul
crypto.summary: The Ethereum Foundation's first PQAI post says AI has become a more urgent risk than quantum computing, with models finding bugs in production software faster than people can review them, and the EF has doubled its protocol security team in response. After more than a year evaluating signature schemes, the EF is advocating hash-based cryptography to replace elliptic curves in three places: hash-based validator keys for consensus, a migration path to hash-based signatures for wallets, and hash-based blob commitments. Justin Drake put forward December 2028 as a target at Devcon, with 2029 as the EF's internal deadline and a timeline review in January, while Ethlabs pulled its Quick Slots proposal out of Hegotá to free up engineering time. The EF calls the upgrade harder than the Merge and warns that BLS tooling, pre-quantum contracts, wallets, multisigs, and staking pools all need changes.

crypto.title: Cross River Bank enters Bitcoin-backed lending with $250K loans
crypto.summary: Cross River Bank and LendingUSA launched a Bitcoin-backed lending program on November 23, offering loans from $10,000 to $250,000 with LTV options at 30%, 50%, or 70% of collateral value. Borrowers can make interest-only payments or defer until maturity, though a BTC price decline triggers additional collateral requirements and potential liquidation of pledged holdings custodied by a qualified third party. This marks Cross River's first entry as a Bitcoin loan originator, adding FDIC-insured bank competition to an existing market that includes Ledn, Coinbase through Morpho, Column N.A. via Strike, and Fortis Bank through Unchained.

crypto.title: Binance Hires Platforms for Independent Security Reviews
crypto.summary: Binance engaged Google Cloud's Mandiant, blockchain security firm SlowMist, and Verichains to run comprehensive, independent reviews of its security procedures, validating current infrastructure and assessing its security posture going forward. CSO Jimmy Su said Binance is committed to acting on what the firms find, and co-CEO Richard Teng called user asset security the exchange's "first responsibility." The announcement covers only the engagement, with no published scope, completion date, or commitment to release findings. It comes 25 days after the intrusion on October 29 that took more than $6 billion and that the DOJ attributes to North Korean actors, which the release does not mention.

crypto.title: UK Bars Crypto Exchanges From Market Making on Their Own Platforms
crypto.summary: HM Treasury made S.I. 2026/1219 on November 18, adding Article 9UA, which excludes dealing as a market maker on a qualifying cryptoasset trading platform (QCATP) from the regulated activity of dealing in qualifying cryptoassets as principal. The FCA's final rule CRYPTO 6.6.1R bars a QCATP operator from executing orders against its proprietary capital on the platform it runs, and guidance CRYPTO 6.6.4G states the operator cannot act as a market maker there. Operators can still use matched principal trading for client orders under non-discretionary rules and deal as principal away from their own venue, but must identify, monitor, and disclose market makers and any liquidity incentive schemes. The rules take effect with the UK's new crypto regime on October 25, 2027.

crypto.title: Monad's first year: what the teams have built since mainnet
crypto.summary: A one-year anniversary article crediting the teams behind Monad. Consensus work progressed from MonadBFT to Cadence, with Quantum Cadence making safety independent of signatures. Other work includes BTX threshold encryption for an encrypted mempool, APES ordering preferences, a zkVM, Private Settlement Domains, MIP-8 page-aware storage pricing, and passkey-derived accounts. Ecosystem figures: 885 teams in the Metropolis hackathon and $82M of weekly tokenized equities volume, up 90% week over week. Visa added Monad to its stablecoin settlement program, Rain supports cards on it, and MetaMask runs its Money Account earn and card program there.

crypto.title: Stellar's Bell (Protocol 30) Brings Smart Accounts and Quantum-Safe Signatures
crypto.summary: Stellar's Protocol 30 upgrade, Bell, is live on mainnet following the validator vote on November 23. CAP-84 adds muxed contract addresses, a new "W" format carrying a 64-bit ID, so one smart account can hold funds for many customers in an omnibus model instead of one contract per customer, and CAP-87 lets smart contracts verify NIST's ML-DSA post-quantum signatures natively inside Stellar Core. CAP-88 moves ledger close times to a millisecond clock, removing the one-second floor so future upgrades can push block times below the current 5 seconds. Network transaction signatures stay Ed25519, and indexers or explorers that decode raw ledger data must update their XDR definitions because the ledger header format changes.

crypto.title: Ondo uses Open USD for instant USDY subscriptions and redemptions
crypto.summary: Open USD (OUSD) is now the default stablecoin for minting and redeeming Ondo's USDY on Tempo.

crypto.title: BTCS Sells 27,300 ETH to Cut Aave Debt 81%
crypto.summary: Nasdaq-listed BTCS sold about 27,300 ETH on November 20 to repay $43.8M of Aave loans, leaving roughly $10.5M of Aave debt at about 32% loan-to-value.

crypto.title: 10,000+ vertical neobanks will launch over the next decade
crypto.summary: Neobanks are being built for narrow customer groups such as real estate agents, medical offices, immigrant communities, music artists and labels, staffing agencies, and restaurant owners.

crypto.title: Onchain options hit a record month at $170M premium
crypto.summary: Onchain options saw $170.1M of premium over 30 days, $1.99B in open interest, and $1B in all-time premium.

it.title: Vibe-coded software has caused a technical debt explosion
it.summary: Appian research found that 96% of surveyed IT leaders expect AI-generated applications to increase technical debt. Faster development is creating unexpected costs around maintenance, troubleshooting, integrations, and ongoing application support.

it.title: Amazon's Decart acquisition is a bet on using software to narrow the silicon gap with Nvidia
it.summary: Amazon is acquiring Decart's team and optimization technology. The deal could improve Trainium performance and give AWS customers more alternatives to Nvidia's GPUs.

it.title: Microsoft declares 'Code Red' after historic outage, internal memos show
it.summary: Microsoft is overhauling its engineering and incident response practices following a 24-hour-long Microsoft 365 outage earlier this month. The company is targeting worldwide recovery within one hour for future incidents, with improvements to traffic isolation, patch deployment, and diagnostics.

it.title: The SaaS resiliency bill is coming due
it.summary: The recent Microsoft outage exposed how deeply enterprise applications depend on external cloud services, even when installed locally. Organizations rarely account for these hidden dependencies when evaluating software purchases. Business continuity planning needs to consider whether entire business processes can survive vendor outages, rather than simply relying on individual service availability guarantees.

it.title: What to remember when offboarding an employee
it.summary: Recent research found that 44% of former employees could still access company systems after leaving. IT leaders recommend automating offboarding, reclaiming software licenses, monitoring post-departure login attempts, and establishing reliable equipment recovery processes. The same identity lifecycle principles increasingly apply to non-human identities, including AI agents.

it.title: Observability is becoming its own data swamp
it.summary: IT organizations are collecting unprecedented volumes of logs, metrics, traces, and alerts, yet often struggle to identify the root cause of incidents. Excessive telemetry is driving up infrastructure costs, slowing investigations, and contributing to alert fatigue. Observability strategies should prioritize actionable signals and business impact over data collection and dashboard proliferation.

it.title: Legacy Modernization with LLMs: Is a large translation consistent with itself?
it.summary: An analysis of a million-line legacy modernization project translated using LLMs revealed that while the generated code appears uniform at first glance, it suffers from significant consistency issues. Independent agent sessions fail to refactor earlier work, introduce style drifts, and frequently rewrite duplicate utility helpers instead of utilizing shared runtime components. Additionally, the LLM autonomously created several basic Python code generators that successfully converted most declarative assets but left behind subtle behavioral discrepancies.

it.summary: Claude Ship is a new tool designed to automate pull request reviews, fixes, and approval decisions to help development teams ship code as fast as they write it. it.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
it.summary: Cisco and OpenAI have launched an open-source project called Shirudo designed to protect running Linux systems from cyberattacks at machine speed. Shirudo intends to provide a defensive window for security teams to develop and deploy permanent patches while the system remains protected.

it.title: Inside an AI-Accelerated Workday Payroll-Diversion Campaign
it.summary: Researchers analyzing security telemetry from recent payroll-diversion campaigns found that attackers took over employee Workday accounts to submit unauthorized direct-deposit changes within seconds of signing in. The telemetry demonstrates rigid browser scripting with invariant two-second pauses between banking actions, while security analysts assess that AI likely assisted in building and running the automation.

it.title: T Brew Movie Club: ‘Johnny Mnemonic' (1995)
it.summary: A look back at the 1995 cyberpunk movie reveals surprisingly relevant lessons about storage capacity, encrypted data transfers, and information security. While the film's once-futuristic 320 GB storage requirement seems modest today, its depiction of capacity constraints and separating decryption credentials from protected data remains relevant.

it.title: Probing DNS at Cloudflare
it.summary: Cloudflare describes how it extended its edge testing framework, Flamingo, with a DNS module to continuously probe production DNS performance and propagation delays. By running automated tests from every data center against authoritative nameservers and public resolvers, the team can detect issues and automatically block rollouts before failures impact customers.

it.title: Beyond a launcher: a new way to interact with Ubuntu
it.summary: Ubuntu developers are previewing a new unified interaction model for the desktop environment, moving beyond a traditional launcher to integrate search, applications, and smart assistance.

it.title: Microsoft refreshes Copilot app search for users without an AI subscription
it.summary: Microsoft is rolling out an updated search experience for Microsoft 365 users without paid Copilot licenses.

it.title: Google Warns Autonomous AI Cyberattacks Are Here: Can Enterprise Defenses Keep Up?
it.summary: Attackers are automating parts of cyberattacks using AI agents, increasing pressure on enterprise patching and incident response processes.

hardware.title: Tesla and SpaceX reportedly aim to sign an all-stock merger by year-end, creating a roughly $3.5 trillion company
hardware.summary: The FT says talks are moving toward a December 31 target, just before a new Congress where Democrats have vowed to probe Musk's companies, even though people familiar say an agreement isn't close. It would need more than 50% of all outstanding Tesla votes, where Musk holds about 20% of voting power, while he controls about 84% of SpaceX. Regulators in the US, China, Europe, and the UK could scrutinize it.

hardware.title: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
hardware.summary: Nvidia's board says Jensen Huang's candor and the input of US officials left them confident his return poses no national security risk, despite the pending independent director investigation into the foreign intelligence effort targeting him. The company is searching for a new Chief Compliance Officer, who will report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, alongside the independent National Security and Export Control Committee formed last week.

hardware.title: Ariane 64 launches 36 Amazon Leo satellites to about 460 km on its second flight with longer P160C boosters, Ariane 6's 10th straight success
hardware.summary: The mission ran 2 hours and 4 minutes from liftoff to final satellite separation, bringing Arianespace's total to 136 Amazon Leo satellites this year. Amazon has ordered six more Ariane 64 launches, for 24 contracted overall.

hardware.title: Uber and Nuro begin driverless testing of Lucid Gravity robotaxis in the Bay Area ahead of a Q1 2027 commercial launch
hardware.summary: The Gravity robotaxi uses high-resolution cameras, solid-state lidar, and radar running Nuro's driver, and testing has moved to no human at the wheel more than six months after California issued the driverless permit. Lucid is starting to build the first production versions at its Arizona factory, expanding the combined test fleet that stood at 100 vehicles earlier this year. Uber will own and operate the fleet and has committed to at least 20,000 Gravity SUVs over six years.

hardware.title: PsiQuantum CEO Victor Peng says quantum is a new form of computing that will create whole new industries, while governments are still catching up
hardware.summary: Peng became CEO in February, more than a year after the Australian federal and Queensland governments signed an AU$900 million deal with PsiQuantum to build a first-of-its-kind quantum computer near Brisbane. He echoes co-founder Mark Thompson's claim that quantum will dwarf AI in impact, and says many in government find that hard to grasp, though some parts have physicists and deeply technical staff.

hardware.title: Insect-size flying robots could leave the lab within two years, but onboard power, sensing, and control are the bottleneck
hardware.summary: University of Washington's Sawyer Fuller predicts a fully autonomous insect-size flyer could fly free soon, though techniques from larger drones break down at this scale and onboard controllers and sensors add weight. MIT's wing-halved design hovered for about 1,000 seconds, 100 times longer than prior bots, and leaves room for batteries and sensors. Other designs, like FVW-Fly, control altitude but still lack directional control.

hardware.title: Bambu Lab's P3C brings a seven-tool changer to a $1,149 printer, about half the price of the H3C
hardware.summary: Instead of purging one nozzle on every color change, the Swaptek system swaps between separate nozzles in about six seconds, with five 0.4 mm tools included and two open slots that cost $99 each to fill. The build volume is 256 x 256 x 260 mm versus 330 x 320 x 325 mm on the H3C, and the bundled AMS 3P loads filament manually, which is the main compromise. It went on sale on November 24, with the seven-tool kit at $1,299.

hardware.title: LLMs handle Verilog but not layouts or waveforms, and agents multiply load on design data systems by 10 to 20x
hardware.summary: Public RTL is plentiful, but models have never seen layouts, and a terabyte waveform database must be converted to text, burning tokens, so panelists want queryable abstractions. Each engineer directing 10 to 20 agents scales version control, NFS, and license demand the same way, and IP governance is a worry. Customers are drifting back from air-gapped open models toward frontier ones, while hybrid specialized models may handle things like temporal assertions.

hardware.title: TSMC files a Texas tax-break application for a $22.6B, 3,232-acre 2nm-and-beyond fab campus in Brazos County, with construction targeted for 2027 to 2031
hardware.summary: The filing proposes at least one logic fab for AI, HPC, and mobile chips and up to 2,099 direct jobs.

hardware.summary: Schumer's X post compares the alleged shipments to "selling rocket engines to the Soviets".

hardware.title: NVIDIA's SSD Writing Bug Needs Another Hotfix as Issue Returns
hardware.summary: NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 40 series experiences ongoing excessive SSD writing, despite the recent GeForce Hotfix 621.35 reducing peak rates.

hardware.title: The White House asks Congress for $2 billion more for Artemis in the next stopgap funding bill, or its activities "would be delayed"
hardware.summary: The ask is one of a list of exemptions, called anomalies, to a funding freeze.
